blockingIssues.description: Bug in /root/benchmark-scripts/coding_agent_bench.py line 391: aggregate_decode_tok_per_s is computed using sum(per-request decode_time_ms) as denominator instead of wall clock time. For concurrency > 1, this reports per-user throughput instead of system aggregate throughput. At concurrency=4, Qwen3.5-9B true aggregate is ~82 tok/s but 21.68 tok/s is reported (3.8x discrepancy). At concurrency=2, true aggregate is ~41 tok/s but 21.71 is reported. This invalidates the aggregate throughput baseline needed for optimization milestone comparisons.
blockingIssues.suggestedFix: In coding_agent_bench.py line 391, replace `aggregate_decode_tok_per_s = total_decode_tokens / (total_decode_time / 1000)` with `aggregate_decode_tok_per_s = total_decode_tokens / (end_time - start_time)` where end_time and start_time are the wall clock benchmark start/end times.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add a note under Coding Conventions: 'When computing aggregate throughput for concurrent benchmarks, use wall clock time as denominator: total_tokens / wall_clock_seconds. Do NOT use sum(per-request decode times) which gives per-user throughput regardless of concurrency.'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: coding_agent_bench.py contains this exact bug (line 391) which was not caught because the AGENTS.md has no guidance on throughput metric calculation. The run-baseline-benchmarks worker (skillFeedback.followedProcedure=true) didn't notice the issue either.
